name: P-wave asystole (ventricular standstill)
stem: Pulseless; monitor shows only small bumps.
action: Treat as asystole: CPR, epinephrine
Pacing is not recommended in arrest

name: Sinus rhythm with ventricular trigeminy
action: Correct the cause: K⁺, hypoxia, ischemia
Monitor

name: CPR artifact
action: You cannot interpret a rhythm during compressions
Analyze during the planned 2-minute pause (< 10 s)

name: Pacemaker spikes with no capture (underlying asystole)
action: This is cardiac arrest: start CPR
Treat as asystole; place pads ≥ 8 cm from the device

name: AV sequential (dual-chamber) paced rhythm
rows: Paced P after each atrial spike
Two per beat — atrial and ventricular
action: Both chambers paced and captured
Normal function

name: Sinus rhythm with demand (VVI) ventricular pacing
stem: Sinus rate slows; pacemaker takes over.
rows: Present on the first 3 beats only
action: Demand pacing: fires only when the native rate falls
Normal sensing and capture

name: 2nd-degree AV block type I (Wenckebach), 5:4
action: Look for digoxin toxicity
Monitor; treat if symptomatic

name: Ventricular tachycardia (rapid)
stem: Patient pale, diaphoretic, BP 70 systolic — has a pulse.
action: Unstable VT with a pulse: synchronized cardioversion 100 J
Sedate if time allows; amiodarone after

name: Idioventricular rhythm
action: Ventricular escape — the heart's last back-up
Do NOT suppress with antiarrhythmics; pace / support perfusion

name: 2nd-degree AV block type II (Mobitz II), 4:3
action: High risk of complete block
Pads on, prepare to pace, transport to PCI/cardiac centre

name: 2nd-degree AV block, 2:1 conduction (wide)
action: Wide QRS → likely infranodal (behaves like Mobitz II)
Pads on; pacing if unstable

name: Transcutaneous pacing WITHOUT capture
stem: Pacing at 70/min, 40 mA; patient remains hypotensive.
rows: Pacer spikes regular; slow escape beats unrelated
Large artifacts not followed by QRS
action: Increase mA until each spike is followed by a wide QRS
Check pad position (anterior–posterior)

name: Junctional rhythm
action: Junctional escape (40–60/min)
Treat as bradycardia if symptomatic; review medications

name: 2nd-degree AV block type II (Mobitz II), 3:2
action: Unstable — pads on, transcutaneous pacing
Atropine unlikely to work; don't delay pacing

name: Accelerated junctional rhythm
action: Rate 60–100 from the junction
Consider digoxin toxicity; monitor

name: Agonal rhythm
stem: Arrest, 25 min of resuscitation, no ROSC.
action: Dying heart — treat as PEA if pulseless
Often a terminal rhythm; consider TOR with medical direction

name: Transcutaneous pacing with electrical capture
stem: You are pacing a patient in complete heart block.
rows: Wide, with large T wave after each spike
Large pacing artifacts at the set rate
action: Electrical capture confirmed — now check a FEMORAL pulse
Give analgesia / sedation

name: Atrial-sensed, ventricular paced rhythm
stem: Pacemaker patient walking briskly — rate rises.
action: Device tracks the sinus rate (DDD/VDD)
Normal function

name: Coarse ventricular fibrillation
stem: Witnessed collapse in a shopping centre; pulseless.
action: Shock immediately, resume CPR 2 min
Epinephrine after initial shocks fail; amiodarone / lidocaine

name: Pacemaker failure to pace (oversensing)
stem: Pacemaker patient with a syncopal episode.
action: Device sensed 'noise' and withheld pacing → pause
Pads on; TCP if pauses recur or unstable

name: 2nd-degree AV block type I (Wenckebach), 4:3
action: Benign in athletes / high vagal tone
Monitor only

name: VT degenerating into VF
stem: Patient with a pulse loses consciousness during the strip.
action: Now pulseless and shockable: defibrillate
Begin VF/pVT algorithm

name: Sinus rhythm with multifocal PVCs
rows: Narrow; PVCs of two different shapes
action: Multifocal = irritable myocardium
Fix hypoxia, check electrolytes, 12-lead

name: 3rd-degree (complete) AV block, junctional escape
action: Junctional escape is more stable
Pads on; atropine may be tried; pace if unstable

name: Polymorphic VT — torsades de pointes
stem: On methadone, long QT history; collapses.
action: Pulseless: defibrillate (unsynchronized)
Magnesium sulfate 1–2 g IV/IO

name: Asystole
stem: Found unresponsive, cool to touch; CPR started.
action: Confirm in 2 leads; check leads and gain
CPR + epinephrine ASAP; consider TOR criteria

name: Pacemaker failure to sense (undersensing)
rows: Fixed rate, some land on QRS/T
action: Spikes fire regardless of native beats — risk of R-on-T
Monitor, transport; ensure pads are ready

name: Pulseless electrical activity (PEA)
stem: Monitor shows this — but NO carotid or femoral pulse.
action: Organized rhythm + no pulse = PEA
CPR, epinephrine ASAP, hunt H's & T's (narrow + fast → mechanical cause)

name: Sinus bradycardia
action: Asymptomatic: no treatment
If symptomatic: atropine 1 mg IV, then pacing / infusion

name: Advanced (high-grade) AV block, 3:1
action: High-grade block — treat like complete heart block
Transcutaneous pacing; epinephrine / dopamine bridge

name: Sinus arrhythmia
rows: Upright, identical, one before each QRS
action: Normal variant, common in the young
No treatment

name: Ventricular paced rhythm (100% capture)
stem: History of complete heart block; feels well.
action: Normal ventricular pacing
Wide paced QRS hides STEMI — use clinical picture / Sgarbossa

name: Fine ventricular fibrillation
stem: Unwitnessed arrest, ~10 min down-time; CPR in progress.
action: Still shockable — defibrillate
Confirm it isn't asystole: check leads and gain

name: Sinus rhythm with sinus arrest (pause)
action: Symptomatic pauses suggest sick sinus syndrome
Pads on; atropine / pacing if symptomatic

name: Sinus tachycardia
action: A response, not a primary problem — treat the cause
Fever, sepsis, hypovolemia, pain, hypoxia

name: Sinus rhythm with a PVC couplet
action: Couplets suggest an irritable ventricle
Monitor closely; 12-lead; treat ischemia

name: 2nd-degree AV block type I (Wenckebach), 3:2
action: Usually nodal, often transient
Atropine if symptomatic

name: Sinus tachycardia
rows: Upright, close to the preceding T
action: Compensating for hypovolemia — don't slow it down
Hemorrhage control, fluids/blood, rapid transport

name: Sinus rhythm with a unifocal PVC
rows: Regular except for one early beat
Absent before the early wide beat
Narrow; the PVC is wide and bizarre
action: Isolated PVCs: treat the patient, not the ectopy
Check K⁺/Mg²⁺ risk, ischemia, hypoxia

name: Monomorphic ventricular tachycardia
action: Pulseless VT = shock (defibrillation dose)
With a pulse and unstable: synchronized 100 J

name: Atrial paced rhythm
stem: Patient has a pacemaker for sick sinus syndrome.
rows: Each P preceded by a pacer spike
action: Normal atrial pacing — device working
Ask for device card; note rate

name: Sinus bradycardia with 1st-degree AV block
action: Watch for progression in inferior MI
Atropine only if symptomatic

name: Sinus rhythm with 1st-degree AV block
action: Benign conduction delay; monitor
Note AV-nodal blocking medications

name: Normal sinus rhythm
stem: 58-year-old, dizzy after standing; now feels well.
action: Normal rhythm — look for a non-cardiac cause of the dizziness
Orthostatic vitals, glucose, history

name: 3rd-degree (complete) AV block, ventricular escape
action: Unstable: transcutaneous pacing now
Infusion bridge: epinephrine 2–10 mcg/min or dopamine

name: Accelerated idioventricular rhythm (AIVR)
stem: Occurs 10 min after successful reperfusion in a STEMI patient.
action: Classic reperfusion rhythm; usually transient
Do not treat with antiarrhythmics if perfusing

name: 2nd-degree AV block, 2:1 conduction (narrow)
action: Type can't be determined from 2:1 alone
Narrow QRS → likely nodal; atropine may help

name: Ventricular pacing with failure to capture
rows: Wide when captured; absent after some spikes
Regular — not all followed by QRS
action: Malfunction: lead displacement, battery, high threshold, hyperkalemia
Transcutaneous pacing if unstable; transport

name: Sinus rhythm with ventricular bigeminy
rows: Regularly irregular — every other beat early
action: Consider ischemia, electrolytes, digoxin
12-lead ECG; monitor for runs of VT

name: 3rd-degree (complete) AV block, slow ventricular escape
stem: Found on floor, GCS 11, BP 64 palpable.
action: Peri-arrest: pace immediately
Prepare for arrest; consider hyperkalemia / drug toxicity
